On-Chain Operator. Lesson 8.1, DeFi portfolio construction. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already pull a number off a chain. The operating system is what you do with it: a register, a journal, and a kill rule.
Buckets: liquidity reserve · core (simple, durable) · productive (LP, vaults, carry) · speculative (new, points, experiments).
Concentration caps: per protocol, per chain, per stablecoin issuer, per bridge.
Genuine diversification: two front ends on the same protocol, or two stablecoins with the same backing, are one risk, not two.
Rebalancing rules: thresholds that trigger moving money between buckets.

Check yourself. 1. Two stablecoins backed by the same collateral: diversified? The answer: No. They share one failure point.
Check yourself. 2. Why keep a reserve bucket? The answer: To defend debt, meet needs and redeploy without forced selling.
Check yourself. 3. When should you rebalance? The answer: When buckets drift past the threshold, or after an incident.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to split capital into risk buckets with caps, so no single failure can sink the portfolio.
First, Buckets: liquidity reserve times core (simple, durable) , productive (L.P., vaults, carry) , speculative (new, points, experiments).
Next, Concentration caps: per protocol, per chain, per stablecoin issuer, per bridge.
Then, Genuine diversification: two front ends on the same protocol, or two stablecoins with the same backing, are one risk, not two.
And finally, Rebalancing rules: thresholds that trigger moving money between buckets.
Rebalance when any bucket drifts more than 5 points from target, or after any incident.
Reserve, 15%, Stablecoins split across 2 issuers, instant access, n/a.
Core, 45%, Blue-chip stable lending (2 protocols), ETH staking, 20%.
Productive, 30%, Wide concentrated L.P., a vault, a P.T., 10%.
Speculative, at most 10%, Points, new protocols, 5%.
